learningObjective: From ptxas register report and launch configuration, derive the register-file-limited theoretical occupancy on a given GPU architecture.

canonicalClaims.claim: Register-limited theoretical occupancy is computed by (⌊register_file_per_SM / (regs_per_thread × threads_per_block)⌋ × threads_per_block) / max_threads_per_SM, expressed as a warp fraction.
conditions: The kernel does not exceed shared-memory-per-SM or block-count-per-SM limits.
Register allocation is per-thread (not per-warp) and rounded per the architecture's granularity.
nonImplications: Does not imply that theoretical occupancy equals achieved occupancy at runtime.
Does not imply that higher occupancy always produces higher throughput.

sourceMappings.locator: Compute capability 8.0: register file 65,536, max threads 2,048/SM, max 32 blocks/SM

misconceptions.claim: Occupancy is limited by the number of blocks per SM (fixed at 8 on all GPUs) regardless of register usage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Block-count-per-SM depends on compute capability (e.g., 32 on sm_80); and register file often binds much earlier than the block-count cap.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, compute capability tables

misconceptions.claim: Higher register usage per thread is always bad because it lowers occupancy and therefore lowers throughput.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Higher per-thread register budget can enable more math per thread, reducing memory traffic and total launched threads; occupancy alone doesn't predict throughput.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: PMPP4; CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide

misconceptions.claim: Register file per SM is 32,768 on all Ampere GPUs, so 96 registers × 256 threads permits only one block per SM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: sm_80 (A100) has 65,536 registers per SM, not 32,768; the correct block count is 2.

misconceptions.claim: Register spills to local memory always improve performance because they free registers for more warps.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Spills touch L1/L2/global memory and are usually costlier than the occupancy gain; the CUDA Best Practices Guide flags spills as a major performance red flag.

implementationFacts: sm_80 register file per SM: 65,536 × 32-bit registers = 256 KB
sm_80 max threads per SM: 2,048 (64 warps)
sm_80 max concurrent blocks per SM: 32
performanceScenarios: A register-heavy kernel (>= 64 regs/thread) with a large block size often runs at 25-50% occupancy on Ampere; this is not automatically a bottleneck.
